title: Muscle-group blending
summary: Aim movements are driven by a primary muscle group but still rely on smooth support from the others, with smaller groups initiating and larger groups following through.
cues: Let the smaller group start the movement and the larger group continue it
Blend transitions so there is no obvious delay between groups
Treat arm, wrist, and fingertips as cooperating layers, not isolated modes
failureModes: Trying to isolate one muscle group completely
Noticeable delay when switching from a smaller correction to a larger follow-through
